subject.title: [Bug]: Tool stdout leaks to chat + reply generation interrupted

question: What boundary should OpenClaw enforce between internal exec stdout, verbose/full debug progress, and external channel-visible replies for this class of runs?
rationale: The current source supports debug tool-output delivery and deliberately avoids replaying side-effectful turns; changing either behavior can affect security expectations and side-effect safety.

options.title: Define narrow suppression and retry policy
options.body: Keep verbose/full as an explicit debug surface, but add a maintainer-approved rule for internal-script stdout and safe post-tool retry cases with focused tests.

options.title: Split into two canonical trackers
options.body: Keep this issue for stdout visibility and route the DeepSeek final-response half entirely to the existing replay-safety issue.

options.title: Keep current debug behavior
options.body: Maintain the documented verbose/full output behavior and require reporters to use message-tool/visibility config or plugin-side filtering for WeChat.

recommendation.title: Define narrow suppression and retry policy
recommendation.body: Keep verbose/full as an explicit debug surface, but add a maintainer-approved rule for internal-script stdout and safe post-tool retry cases with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the verbose feedback path and merged the adjacent post-tool recovery work, making him the strongest routing candidate for the boundary decision.
